clue.text: Drunken revellers taking taxi back sing — couple from Essex

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the word for a taxi around, since it follows 'taxi'
a couple from Essex means its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Boozy partygoers hail a cab home, singing, with a couple of Essex lads in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAB into BAC; 'couple from' takes the first two letters of Essex, ES. The followers of Bacchus, god of wine, were famed for drunken revels.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth these were the frenzied female worshippers of Bacchus, god of wine, given to wild drinking.

clue.text: Blow the expert!

definitions.meaning: an old word for a punch or stroke
an enthusiast with deep knowledge, as in a film or wine fanatic

explanation.surface: An exasperated curse aimed at a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic name for a blow, and also means a knowledgeable fan of some subject.

clue.text: It's smart carrying a knife

indicators.note: carrying means the word for smart holds the next piece inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that a well-dressed person is armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like 'well dressed' but means CLEVER; 'carrying' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's heavy chopping blade is a kind of knife.

clue.text: Like certain insects-could some hornet, yup?

indicators.note: could suggests the letters might be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a hornet is a particular kind of insect, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of SOME HORNET YUP could form the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees, wasps, ants and sawflies belong to the insect order with membranous wings, and this adjective describes them.

clue.text: Number of home that's out this world in the Big Apple

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York, NY
home means in, as in 'staying in'
out of this world suggests an extraterrestrial, ET

explanation.surface: A house number that is described as heavenly in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' is a nickname for an alien, from the film character; the clue as held has lost its 'of'. 'in' works twice over in the surface, but only the second signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cardinal figure, nine times ten.

clue.text: English doctor made rapid progress to get accepted enthusiastically

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: An English physician quickly rose through the ranks and was warmly welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an idea or person eagerly is to hug it to oneself, figuratively.

clue.text: There'll be one on the staff very familiar to 22

definitions.text: There'll be one on the staff very familiar to 22

parts.words: There'll be one on the staff very familiar to 22
parts.note: the staff is the five-line musical stave, and a music graduate (22 across) knows the sign placed at its start well

explanation.surface: An employee who is well known to a senior academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but here it is the musical stave; the sign at its start fixes pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble or bass, this symbol sits at the left of every stave to fix the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: American city set joining Scot who lives in ex-Communist country?

parts.note: a set is a television, TV
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name, standing for any Scot

explanation.surface: A man from Los Angeles joins a Scot and settles in a former Soviet state.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN as a stand-in for a Scotsman is a crossword convention. The country is a Baltic state once part of the USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Baltic republic of Riga, once in the Soviet Union, bears this name.

clue.text: Suffering demise, foul rodent

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are tormented out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature dies a nasty, painful death.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild mouse of fields and woods, a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Old DJ who never worked slavishly?

definitions.meaning: Alan 'Fluff' ... was a veteran BBC Radio 1 disc jockey
a person who has never been a slave, free from bondage

explanation.surface: A veteran radio presenter who never toiled like a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: The DJ is Alan 'Fluff' Freeman, a long-serving BBC radio presenter famed for Pick of the Pops.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan 'Fluff' Freeman was a famous British radio presenter; the word also names a citizen not in bondage.

clue.text: About to go in to swim? Do this before you go under

definitions.text: Do this before you go under

indicators.note: to go in tells us the word for about is placed inside the word for swim

explanation.surface: Advice to a swimmer about to dive: take a gulp of air first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to go in' reads as 'on the point of entering', but 'About' is RE and 'to go in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Before ducking under water you take in air, a cryptic hint at drawing a lungful.

clue.text: See best man Sam err badly accounts for red faces

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A best man called Sam blunders his speech, causing blushes all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing is the sign of feeling awkward and ashamed.

clue.text: Type of screen, invented in lab, with moving parts

indicators.note: moving parts suggests the letters shift about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screen developed in a laboratory that has mechanical parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of INVENTED IN LAB give a slatted screen, which itself has moving parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A window covering of adjustable horizontal slats is a kind of screen.

clue.text: Police raid — when this mag very naughty?

indicators.note: very naughty suggests the letters misbehave, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police raid a publisher, wondering if the magazine was too racy.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a publication issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Regret about optimism beginning to fade in several countries

indicators.note: about tells us the word for regret is turned round
beginning to fade means the opening letter of the word for optimism disappears

explanation.surface: Sorrow as hope fades across a group of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RUE to EUR; 'beginning to fade' drops the H of HOPE to leave OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is made up of many nations.

clue.text: Attack brings sign of sadness in time, then nothing

parts.note: a tear is a sign of sadness

explanation.surface: A tearful moment followed by emptiness, then an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone, physically or verbally, is to assault them.

clue.text: There's endless tea in unsatisfactory musical work

indicators.note: in places the shortened tea inside the word for unsatisfactory
endless means the final letter of the tea's name is dropped

parts.note: bohea is a type of black China tea

explanation.surface: A complaint that the music was poor, with endless tea breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohea is an old name for a black China tea, little known outside crosswords; 'endless' drops its final letter before 'in' sets it inside the word for poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about Parisian bohemians is a musical work.

clue.text: Wobbly hat being secured

indicators.note: wobbly suggests the letters are shaken unsteadily, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loose hat being fastened down.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a result that is certain or already won.

clue.text: Gets stuck into the French food first

indicators.note: first tells us the word for food comes before the French article

parts.note: tack is food, as in hard tack, a ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone tucks eagerly into French food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets stuck into' looks like eating, but means takes on with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To get stuck into a task is to grapple with it.

clue.text: Material produced by nutty artists

explanation.surface: Fabric made by crazy painters.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a common crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, often checked cotton fabric named after an Indian city.

clue.text: Get education about religious matters going to church? I have!

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having had a religious schooling and gone to church.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, the school subject in Britain; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To take delivery of something is to be given it.

clue.text: Pre-1922 port Mary's drunk around noon

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for noon
drunk suggests the letters reel about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive here supplies an S along with the name

explanation.surface: Mary is tipsy by midday in an old harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles MARYS, which goes 'around' N (noon). The Aegean port was renamed Izmir after 1922.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek port in Anatolia was burnt in 1922 and is now Izmir, Turkey.

clue.text: A noted senior academic

parts.note: noted means having to do with musical notes, so the senior academic is a holder of the top music degree

explanation.surface: A distinguished professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like 'famous' but means concerned with musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest university degree in music is a doctorate, held by a senior scholar.

clue.text: Go deficient? Not right!

indicators.note: not right means the abbreviation for right is removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is lacking and wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' drops the R from SHORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is having an attempt.

clue.text: Piece fitted the wrong way in Margaret's electronic instrument

indicators.note: fitted the wrong way means the run of letters is read backwards
piece means a run of letters is taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A component wrongly installed in Margaret's electronic keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' picks letters from 'Margaret's electronic'; 'fitted the wrong way' turns them round. 'electronic' is a red herring: the instrument is a keyboard with hammers striking metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument whose hammers strike steel plates, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Herein's Schumann's Third, not Beethoven's Third which would be wrong

definitions.text: Herein's Schumann's Third, not Beethoven's Third which would be wrong

indicators.note: which would be wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order, so they are rearranged
not tells us one letter is swapped in place of another
third picks the third letter of the composer's name
third picks the third letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A music lover insists the piece here is Schumann's Third symphony, not Beethoven's.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the E (Beethoven's third letter) in HEREINS with H (Schumann's third letter), then rearrange. Schumann's Symphony No 3 is nicknamed the Rhenish.
explanation.definitionFit: Schumann's Symphony No 3 is nicknamed after the Rhine, and the word means of the Rhine.

clue.text: Inclination for a composer's sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer

explanation.surface: A leaning toward a particular composer's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Liszt the composer sounds the same as the word for a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's tilt to one side is a lean or inclination.

clue.text: Go with soldiers to edge of desert-not the whole company

indicators.note: edge of desert here means its final letter

explanation.surface: Troops march off to the edge of the desert, leaving some behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of a firm is only part of the organisation.
